causing it was that I had a Stratum Layer called "Region" which also had an
attributed called "Region". When I changed the attribute name so it was not
the same as the layer name this fixed the problem.

Regards

Nigel Harding

messages.subject: Re: of freedom
messages.body_plain:
Laura V=E1zquez Cast=E1n wrote:
> > I have very little experience using the
> > program Distance Sampling and I have two questions:
> >
> > 1. Why in the
> > degrees of freedom are obtained decimals instead of integers
> >  =20
This is covered in the 2001 distance sampling book.  If you don't have=20
access to that, you'll find the 1993 book on the Distance web pages. =20
The df are a weighted average of the df for encounter rate and the df=20
for estimating f(0).
> > 2. Why the density and the density of the group have the same coefficie=
nt of
> > variation and the same values
> >  =20
They aren't, unless all groups are of the same size, but the cv for mean=20
group size can sometimes be very small, so that they could be the same=20
after rounding.

Steve Buckland

I thought it worth mentioning.

messages.subject: Re: Code analysis of designed experiments with distance data?
messages.subject_clean: Code analysis of designed experiments with distance data?
messages.body_plain:
The Royle et al paper is more related to modelling spatial distance
sampling data (and assumes that distances are grouped into intervals).
There is also code in Distance (the DSM engine) that does something
similar (see Hedley, S.L. and Buckland, S.T. 2004. Spatial models for
line transect sampling. /Journal of Agricultural, Biological and
Environmental Statistics/ *9*, 181-199).  We are currently working on
more sophisticated spatial methods for Distance, based on: Wood, S.N.,
Bravington, M.V. and Hedley, S.L. 2008. Soap film smoothing. JRSS Series B.

We don't currently have documented code for designed experiments in
distance sampling.  We have a research student developing improved
methods (which don't need the two-stage approach of the 2009 paper and
which allow random effects), and hope to get these methods, together
with the methods of the 2009 paper, into Distance, given funding and the
availability of the right programmer ...

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: Distance sampling training workshops, Arusha, Tanzania, Dec 2010
messages.subject_clean: Distance sampling training workshops, Arusha, Tanzania, Dec 2010
messages.body_plain:
Registration is now open for workshops in practical skills for=20
ecologists to be held in Arusha, Tanzania, from the 29th November to=20
11th December.  A summary of the workshops are given below; more=20
information is available at http://www.tzcrc.org/skills/   Please direct=20
any questions to ArushaSkill...@gmail.com

29 Nov=96 1 Dec
** Introduction to GIS (Paul Bessels, Uni. of Glasgow) **
Content: Elements of GIS, creation of maps & intergration of GPS data,=20
spatial analysis. Focusing on QGIS (a free GIS package), this 3 day=20
course will give practical skills in creating maps, understanding=20
cartographic concepts, and basic analysis.
Cost: US$100 for sponsored attendees, $30 for unfunded students.

2 =96 4 Dec
** Repeat of above **

6-8 Dec
** Primer on Distance sampling (Len Thomas, Uni. of St. Andrews) **
Content: This workshop is for any wildlife biologist who wants to=20
design, collect or analyze distance sampling survey data.  The emphasis=20
of the workshop will be on how to design a good survey, how to collect=20
good data and how to do preliminary analyses using pen and paper, a=20
calculator and a computer spreadsheet.  Complete beginners are very=20
welcome.  Those with more experience may (i) benefit from the refresher,=20
(ii) learn something from the detailed discussion of assumptions, how to=20
meet them, and what happens if things go wrong, (iii) be able to use the=20
material as a basis for teaching others.
Cost: US$150

9-11 Dec
** Distance sampling survey design and analysis (Len Thomas) **
Content: A workshop for people who are familiar with the concepts=20
covered on the previous workshop, and who want to analyze survey data=20
using the program Distance.  We will cover more advanced topics such as=20
stratification and variance estimation, as well as real-world survey=20
design.
Cost: US$150

--=20

messages.subject: treatment comparisons within distance
messages.body_plain:
I'm looking for the best way to analyze survey data comparing various =
protocols.
We have conducted an experimental seabird survey with two observers; =
where one was the reference using one protocol all along while the other =
was switching among three protocols to be tested against the reference. =
Since the three protocols were used in blocks (1-hour blocks, 20 min. =
per protocol within a block), I also need to take this random effect =
into account. We did not use capture-recapture because it would be =
impossible to ascertain which bird (or group) was detected or not by the =
two observers.

I'm more from a frequentist background, and modeling this analysis into =
a general linear model and contrast each treatment against the reference =
would be fairly straightforward using a stat package. However, I would =
like to take into account the detection rate, but at the same time I'm =
not looking for the most accurate density and just comparing apparent =
density might be ok too...I wonder however about how all this would =
affect variance estimates, as precision would be one way to judge the =
results.

On top of my head, I see several options:
1- somehow find a way to model all this correctly into Distance;
2- compute the detection function in Distance, somehow apply it to the =
data and analyze the results through a general linear model;
3- run a general linear model using the raw data;
4- others?

Any advice/idea welcome!

Fran=E7ois Bolduc
